title: O, for a Heart to Praise My God
description: O, for a Heart to Praise My God in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 518, “Desires for Holiness”, where the book credits them to a Wesleyan source.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O, for a heart to praise my God, A heart from sin set free; A heart that al-ways feels how good, Thou, Lord, hast been to me.

lines: O, for a heart to praise my God,
A heart from sin set free;
A heart that always feels how good,
Thou, Lord, hast been to me.
O for an humble, trustful heart,
Which neither life nor death can part
A heart in every thought renewed,
Perfect, and right, and pure, and good,
O, write Thy name upon my heart!
Thy name, O God, is love.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1866.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
